readers.program: libsystem and any other user of the inline header function tron::get_repo_root
readers.mechanism: std::getenv in tron::get_repo_root

readers.program: libsystem: resource_map_manager::load_resource_map. Reached by rinzler and its three variants, runtron and tests, outside a Dice grant
readers.mechanism: calls get_repo_root, which reads the variable at h/common/paths.hpp:67

readers.program: libsystem: base_mountpoint inside tron::fuse::default_mountpoint. Reached by rinzler, rinzler_mock, rinzler_host and runtron, not by rinzler_proxy
readers.mechanism: calls get_repo_root, only when the program file path contains /gen/ and RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH is unset or empty

variables.values: Path to a directory. Any non-empty text is used as given. The code does not check that the directory exists.
variables.default: Unset: the repository root is worked out from the path of the running program (/proc/self/exe). The last path part named gen or gen-<variant> marks the build tree. If that tree holds a file .checkout-root, its first line is the root. Otherwise the directory above the build tree is the root. A program outside such a tree has an empty root (h/common/paths.hpp:36-76).
variables.empty_value: Same as unset. The code tests the first character (h/common/paths.hpp:68).
variables.invalid_value: No check and no error. A wrong path only makes the two derived paths fail later. <value>/config/resource-map.yaml does not load, and the search moves to the next candidate. <value>/stats is created if possible; otherwise the warning 'Could not create FUSE mount point' is logged.
variables.effect: Two effects. 1. Resource map (the YAML file that maps each instance to FPGA cards and CPU cores): <value>/config/resource-map.yaml becomes the third candidate of the search. This applies to every build, also an installed one. 2. FUSE stats mount: in a development build (the program file path contains /gen/), with RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH unset or empty and no --fuse-mount flag, the base mount directory becomes <value>/stats.
variables.interactions: Resource map search order: the --resource-map path, resource-map.yaml in the current working directory, <repository root>/config/resource-map.yaml, <program directory>/../config/resource-map.yaml, /opt/positron/config/resource-map.yaml. The first file that loads is used (src/system/resource_map.cpp:84-125). Under a Dice grant (DICE_DAEMON_CHILD=1) the map is loaded only from /opt/positron/config/resource-map.yaml, so the variable has no effect on the map (src/system/system.cpp:1681, 1930-1934). For the FUSE path, --fuse-mount and RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH come first. A build tree named gen-<variant> does not count as a development build for the FUSE path, because is_dev_build looks for the text /gen/ (h/common/paths.hpp:24-27).
variables.how_to_check: No log line prints the variable. The resource map in use is logged as 'INIT: Successfully loaded resource map from <path>, server type: <type>' (src/system/system.cpp:1941). The FUSE path in use is logged as 'Stats/config mounted at <path>' (src/rinzler.cpp:4737, src/runtron.cpp:512).
variables.audience_reason: It redirects paths that are derived from a source checkout. Nothing in the checkout sets it. Operators have --resource-map and RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH for the same two purposes.

variables.name: RZ_CHAT_TEMPLATE_KWARGS

readers.program: rinzler, rinzler_mock, rinzler_host, rinzler_proxy (all four compile src/rinzler.cpp, src/CMakeLists.txt:95, 115, 152, 180)
readers.mechanism: std::getenv in the completions_controller constructor

variables.values: JSON text. The raw text must be at most 512 bytes. It must parse as JSON. The JSON value must be an object. The JSON value null is also accepted and is ignored. Each member value must be a scalar: nested objects and arrays are rejected. These 9 keys are rejected: messages, add_generation_prompt, bos_token, eos_token, tools, strftime_now, tokenize, continue_final_message, documents (h/rinzler/chat-template-reserved-keys.hpp:22-32). reasoning_effort, when not null, must be one of the strings none, low, medium, high, xhigh. enable_thinking, when not null, must be a boolean. Members with a null value are dropped. The checked object, written again as JSON, must also be at most 512 bytes (h/rinzler/rinzler-config.hpp:148-218).
variables.default: Unset: the server defaults are an empty object (DEFAULT_CHAT_TEMPLATE_KWARGS, h/rinzler/rinzler-config.hpp:145). No extra variable reaches a chat template unless a request sends chat_template_kwargs.
variables.empty_value: Not the same as unset. Empty text is not valid JSON. rinzler logs 'RZ_CHAT_TEMPLATE_KWARGS invalid JSON: ...' and exits with code 1.
variables.invalid_value: rinzler logs one error and exits with code 1 before any model is loaded. The three errors are 'RZ_CHAT_TEMPLATE_KWARGS exceeds maximum size of 512 bytes' (src/rinzler.cpp:2396), 'RZ_CHAT_TEMPLATE_KWARGS invalid JSON: ...' (src/rinzler.cpp:2408) and 'RZ_CHAT_TEMPLATE_KWARGS validation failed: ...' (src/rinzler.cpp:2411).
variables.effect: Sets server-wide default chat_template_kwargs (extra variables given to the chat template when the prompt of a chat completion request is rendered). The defaults apply to every chat completion request. They change the rendered prompt, so they also change the prompt token ids.
variables.interactions: chat_template_kwargs in a request override the server defaults key by key (h/rinzler/rinzler-config.hpp:223-232). A null value in a request does not remove a server default. A top-level reasoning_effort in the request overrides both (h/rinzler/rinzler-config.hpp:274-284, used at src/rinzler.cpp:2996). A default reasoning_effort of none or xhigh passes startup, but each Harmony (gpt-oss) request that does not override it is rejected with HTTP 400 (comment at h/rinzler/reasoning-effort.hpp:52-54). README.proxy.md:171-175 says a tokenizer sidecar (a server run with RZ_SAVE_TOKENS_PROMPT_ONLY=1) must use the same value as the serving host.
variables.how_to_check: 'Loaded RZ_CHAT_TEMPLATE_KWARGS: <merged JSON>' at info level (src/rinzler.cpp:2405). The line is absent when the variable is unset.
variables.audience_reason: It changes the prompt that a deployed rinzler renders for every chat request.

variables.name: RZ_ENABLE_SAVE_TOKENS

readers.program: rinzler, rinzler_mock, rinzler_host, rinzler_proxy (all four compile src/rinzler.cpp, src/CMakeLists.txt:95, 115, 152, 180)
readers.mechanism: std::getenv. The raw value is parsed by parse_save_tokens_enabled (h/rinzler/rinzler-config.hpp:290)

variables.values: Exactly the text 1 enables. Exactly the text 0 disables. No other text is accepted.
variables.empty_value: Not the same as unset. Startup fails, because an empty value is neither 0 nor 1.
variables.invalid_value: rinzler logs 'RZ_ENABLE_SAVE_TOKENS validation failed: RZ_ENABLE_SAVE_TOKENS must be "0" or "1" (got: "<value>")' and exits with code 1 (src/rinzler.cpp:2422-2423).
variables.effect: Gates the request parameter save_tokens (a development capture: the response also carries the rendered prompt text, its token ids and the output token ids). With 0, a chat completion request with save_tokens true gets HTTP 400 with the text 'save_tokens' is disabled on this server. A legacy completion request whose body has the key save_tokens with the literal true gets the same answer (src/rinzler.cpp:2722, 2739). Requests without save_tokens are not affected.
variables.interactions: RZ_SAVE_TOKENS_PROMPT_ONLY=1 together with 0 here fails startup. A save_tokens request with stream true is HTTP 400 for every value of this variable (src/rinzler.cpp:2716, 2733). The packaged unit sets the value 1 (packaging/systemd/rinzler@.service:19). The unit loads /opt/positron/user/config.env afterwards (line 43), and README.proxy.md:148-153 names that file as the place to set 0.
variables.how_to_check: With 0: 'save_tokens capture disabled via RZ_ENABLE_SAVE_TOKENS=0' at info level (src/rinzler.cpp:2426). With 1 or unset: no log line. A request with save_tokens true then returns a save_tokens object instead of HTTP 400.
variables.audience_reason: A serving host can switch the capture parameter off without a rebuild. The packaged unit sets it.

readers.program: runtron
readers.mechanism: calls default_mountpoint(instance_idx, instance_total) when --fuse-mount is absent

variables.values: Path to a directory. The text is used as given. The program creates the final directory, with its parents, when it does not exist (ensure_mountpoint, src/system/fuse_helpers.cpp:99-107).
variables.default: Unset: <repository root>/stats when the program file path contains /gen/ and a repository root is found. Otherwise /opt/positron/stats (src/system/fuse_helpers.cpp:30-36).
variables.invalid_value: The text is not checked. If the directory cannot be created, the program logs the warning 'Could not create FUSE mount point <path>: <reason>' and goes on to the mount step. If stats initialization throws, the program prints 'error initializing FUSE stats: ...' and exits with code 1 (src/rinzler.cpp:4731-4733, src/runtron.cpp:507-509). not determined: which mount failures throw. I did not read stats::initialize.
variables.effect: Sets the base directory where rinzler and runtron mount the FUSE stats file system (files that show live statistics and settings). When the process is one of several instances (instance count above 1), /instance-<index> is appended, unless RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PRESCOPED is exactly 1.
variables.interactions: --fuse-mount wins and is used as given, with no instance suffix. RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PRESCOPED=1 removes the suffix. The instance pair comes from --instance on the command line, or from --instance inside SYSTEM_CONFIG when the command line has none (src/system/system.cpp:1024-1027). REPO_ROOT_OVERRIDE changes the fallback path of a development build. rinzler_proxy never mounts, does not read the variable and rejects --fuse-mount (src/rinzler.cpp:129-135, 4335). The packaged unit sets /var/run/rinzler/%i and also expands the variable in its ExecStartPre, ExecStop and ExecStopPost lines (packaging/systemd/rinzler@.service:7, 50-55). The comment at lines 20-25 of the unit says the per-instance file /etc/rinzler/instance-%i.env may override it.
variables.how_to_check: 'FUSE mount point from RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH: <value>' (src/system/fuse_helpers.cpp:27) shows that the variable was used. 'FUSE mount point scoped for instance i,N: <path>' (src/system/fuse_helpers.cpp:93) shows the suffix. 'Stats/config mounted at <path>' (src/rinzler.cpp:4737, src/runtron.cpp:512) shows the final path.
variables.audience_reason: It sets where a deployed rinzler exposes its stats files. The packaged unit and platformd set it.

variables.name: RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PRESCOPED

readers.program: libsystem: tron::fuse::default_mountpoint (rinzler, rinzler_mock, rinzler_host at src/rinzler.cpp:4725; runtron at src/runtron.cpp:491)
readers.mechanism: std::getenv, then comparison with the text 1

variables.values: Exactly the text 1 turns the per-instance suffix off. Every other text leaves the suffix on, for example true, yes or 0.
variables.default: Unset: with an instance count above 1 and an instance index of 0 or more, /instance-<index> is appended to the mount path.
variables.empty_value: Same as unset. The suffix stays on.
variables.invalid_value: No error. Any text other than 1 is treated as off, with no message. The comment at packaging/systemd/rinzler@.service:8-14 says the result in the packaged setup is a wrong mount path (/var/run/rinzler/0/instance-0) and no startup error.
variables.effect: Tells the program that the mount path is already separate for each instance. The program then uses the path without the /instance-<index> suffix.
variables.interactions: It applies to a path from RZ_FUSE_MOUNT_PATH and also to the two built-in fallback paths (src/system/fuse_helpers.cpp:84-87). It has no effect when --fuse-mount is given, when no instance is given, or when the instance count is 1. The packaged unit sets it to 1 (packaging/systemd/rinzler@.service:15). The comment at lines 20-25 of the unit says the per-instance environment file must not set it.
variables.how_to_check: No log line prints the variable. When the suffix is added, the program logs 'FUSE mount point scoped for instance i,N: <path>' (src/system/fuse_helpers.cpp:93). For a multi-instance run, that line is absent and 'Stats/config mounted at <path>' has no /instance-<i> part when the opt-out is in effect or --fuse-mount was given.
variables.audience_reason: The packaged unit depends on it. A wrong value moves the stats mount and breaks the platformd scanner, by the unit comment.

variables.name: RZ_KV_CACHE_GB

readers.program: rinzler, rinzler_mock, rinzler_host, rinzler_proxy (all four compile src/rinzler.cpp, src/CMakeLists.txt:95, 115, 152, 180). runtron does not read it
readers.mechanism: std::getenv in main, then std::stoull

variables.values: A whole number of GiB. The code shifts the number left by 30 bits to get bytes (src/tron/scheduler/token_cache.cpp:458). Parsed with std::stoull, base 10 (src/rinzler.cpp:4578). Leading white space and a + or - sign are accepted. Parsing stops at the first character that is not a digit, so 8GB gives 8 and 1.5 gives 1. 0 gives a target of 0 bytes. -1 wraps to 0xffffffffffffffff, which is the internal marker for 'not set', so the default size applies. I checked these std::stoull results with a stand-alone test program on this host.
variables.default: Unset: the stored value keeps the marker 0xffffffffffffffff (src/system/system.cpp:77). get_kv_cache_size then returns half of the hugepage count, used as a number of GiB (src/system/system.cpp:2539-2545). The hugepage count is 16 unless POS_1GB_PER_NUMA, POS_NR_HUGEPAGES or --nr_hugepages changes it (h/system/config.hpp:12), which gives 8 GiB. In arena allocator mode this size is not used (see interactions).
variables.empty_value: Not the same as unset. rinzler logs 'RZ_KV_CACHE_GB set to '. std::stoull then throws std::invalid_argument. main has no try block around the call. The terminate handler logs a backtrace and calls abort (src/common/backtrace.cpp:33-36, installed at src/rinzler.cpp:4548).
variables.invalid_value: Text that does not start with a number ends the process the same way as an empty value. A number too large for 64 bits throws std::out_of_range, with the same result.
variables.effect: Only in legacy allocator mode: sets the target size of the persistent KV cache (the stored attention keys and values that rinzler keeps between requests). One target covers all models together. In arena allocator mode the value is ignored and a warning is logged.
variables.interactions: 1. Arena allocator mode (pos_heap_v2) ignores the value. The cache target is set to the largest int64 value and one warning is logged (src/tron/scheduler/token_cache_control.cpp:60-88). Arena mode is the build default (option TRON_ARENA_ALLOCATOR_DEFAULT_ON is ON, src/system/CMakeLists.txt:86), and TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR selects the mode at run time (src/system/memory.cpp:93-97). The mode is set in pos_heap_setup, which only the real device library calls (src/pos/driver.cpp:290). So on a default build of rinzler the variable has no effect unless TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR holds a value other than 1. In rinzler_host, rinzler_mock and rinzler_proxy arena mode stays off. rinzler_host contains the token cache code (fake_scheduler_static, src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:431-433), so the value is used there. rinzler_mock and rinzler_proxy read and store the value, but their scheduler libraries do not contain the token cache code (src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:440-452), and I found no user of the value in them. 2. The flag --kv-cache-gb is parsed later and writes the same variable, so the flag wins (src/system/system.cpp:2046-2048). The flag can be on the command line. For the real rinzler it can also be inside SYSTEM_CONFIG. 3. runtron has the flags --kv-cache-gb and --kv-cache-bytes instead (src/runtron.cpp:625-636). 4. The host package drop-in sets the value 1 (packaging/tron-host/90-rinzler-host.conf:19).
variables.how_to_check: 'RZ_KV_CACHE_GB set to <text>' at startup (src/rinzler.cpp:4577) shows the raw text. 'Trying to use <N> GB for persistent KV cache (covering all models)' (src/tron/scheduler/token_cache.cpp:456) shows the number when the cache object is created. That line is also printed in arena mode, where the number is then not used. The warning 'Arena allocator (pos_heap_v2) is active; ignoring static KV cache sizing knob RZ_KV_CACHE_GB' (src/tron/scheduler/token_cache_control.cpp:76-80) shows that the value is ignored.
variables.audience_reason: Memory tuning of a deployed rinzler. A packaged drop-in sets it.
variables.disagreement: The facts agree. The inventory is vague in two fields. Its 'effect' and 'default' read as if the value always applies. The code ignores the value in arena allocator mode, which is the build default for the real rinzler (src/system/CMakeLists.txt:86, src/tron/scheduler/token_cache_control.cpp:60-88). The inventory says this only in 'notes'. Two details are missing: the unit is GiB (shift by 30 bits, src/tron/scheduler/token_cache.cpp:458), and the value -1 wraps to the 'not set' marker, so the default applies.

variables.name: RZ_SAVE_TOKENS_PROMPT_ONLY

readers.program: rinzler, rinzler_mock, rinzler_host, rinzler_proxy (all four compile src/rinzler.cpp, src/CMakeLists.txt:95, 115, 152, 180)
readers.mechanism: std::getenv. The raw value is parsed by parse_save_tokens_prompt_only (h/rinzler/rinzler-config.hpp:305)

variables.values: Exactly the text 1 enables. Exactly the text 0 is off. No other text is accepted. 1 is accepted only when save_tokens is enabled (RZ_ENABLE_SAVE_TOKENS unset or 1).
variables.default: Unset: off. A save_tokens request runs a normal generation.
variables.empty_value: Not the same as unset. Startup fails, because an empty value is neither 0 nor 1.
variables.invalid_value: rinzler logs 'RZ_SAVE_TOKENS_PROMPT_ONLY validation failed: RZ_SAVE_TOKENS_PROMPT_ONLY must be "0" or "1" (got: "<value>")' and exits with code 1. With 1 and RZ_ENABLE_SAVE_TOKENS=0 the message is 'RZ_SAVE_TOKENS_PROMPT_ONLY=1 needs save_tokens, but RZ_ENABLE_SAVE_TOKENS=0' (src/rinzler.cpp:2432-2433, h/rinzler/rinzler-config.hpp:310-316).
variables.effect: With 1, a request that asks for save_tokens passes every request check and is then answered at once. The body holds only the save_tokens object: the rendered prompt text, its token ids, an empty output_tokens list, and rendered_at for chat requests. Nothing is generated. Requests without save_tokens generate as usual (src/rinzler.cpp:3647-3659). The code comments call this the tokenizer sidecar mode.
variables.interactions: Requires RZ_ENABLE_SAVE_TOKENS unset or 1. A save_tokens request with stream true stays HTTP 400. README.proxy.md:181-184 says to set the variable only in the launch environment of the sidecar and not in /opt/positron/user/config.env, because the packaged unit loads that file for every instance on the host.
variables.how_to_check: 'save_tokens requests answer before generation (RZ_SAVE_TOKENS_PROMPT_ONLY=1)' at info level (src/rinzler.cpp:2436-2437). No line when off.
variables.audience_reason: It turns a deployed server into a tokenizer sidecar. A wrong setting stops generation for save_tokens requests.

variables.name: RZ_SYSTEM_START_DATE

readers.program: librinzler: tron::harmony::configure_system_start_date_from_env. The only product caller is the completions_controller constructor at src/rinzler.cpp:2385 (rinzler, rinzler_mock, rinzler_host, rinzler_proxy (all four compile src/rinzler.cpp, src/CMakeLists.txt:95, 115, 152, 180))
readers.mechanism: std::getenv. The checked value is kept in a static, and later requests use the kept value

readers.program: rinzler_proxy (shared library proxy_scheduler): golden_map::validate_rendered_at, called from stream_generate at src/tron/scheduler/proxy.cpp:418
readers.mechanism: std::getenv, then comparison of the raw text with the rendered_at entry of the golden token file

variables.values: A date written as YYYY-MM-DD. Exactly 10 characters. Characters 5 and 8 are '-' and all others are digits (src/rinzler/harmony.cpp:864-870). The date must exist in the calendar of the local time zone. The year must be 1000 or later. The date must be inside the range of std::chrono::system_clock (src/rinzler/harmony.cpp:966-1011). A code comment gives that range as 1677 to 2262 for libstdc++.
variables.default: Unset: no pinned date. Each request uses the local date of today, computed again for each request.
variables.empty_value: Not the same as unset. The format check fails. rinzler logs 'RZ_SYSTEM_START_DATE validation failed: RZ_SYSTEM_START_DATE must be YYYY-MM-DD, got ''' and exits with code 1.
variables.invalid_value: rinzler logs 'RZ_SYSTEM_START_DATE validation failed: <reason>' and exits with code 1 (src/rinzler.cpp:2387-2388). The reasons are: 'RZ_SYSTEM_START_DATE must be YYYY-MM-DD, got '<text>'', 'system start date '<date>' is before year 1000', '... is not a valid calendar date' (for example 2031-02-31), and '... is outside the clock's representable range'.
variables.effect: Pins the date that rinzler writes into prompts, so the same conversation renders to the same token ids on every day. Three places use the pinned date. 1. The conversation_start_date of the Harmony (gpt-oss) system message (src/rinzler/harmony.cpp:1085). 2. The clock of the strftime_now function of Hugging Face chat templates, set to local noon of that date (src/rinzler/hf-token-processor.cpp:680). 3. The rendered_at field of a save_tokens capture.
variables.interactions: In rinzler_proxy, when the golden token file has a rendered_at entry, every generation throws std::runtime_error unless the variable holds exactly that text. An unset variable also throws (src/tron/scheduler/golden_tokens.cpp:223-244). Chat templates that never call strftime_now are not affected (comment at h/rinzler/chat-template-reserved-keys.hpp:11-21). The time zone (TZ) applies, because the code uses mktime and localtime_r. README.proxy.md:171-173 says a tokenizer sidecar must use the same value as the serving host.
variables.how_to_check: No startup log line prints an accepted value. A chat request with save_tokens true returns the date in save_tokens.rendered_at (src/rinzler.cpp:1274). A bad value is reported by 'RZ_SYSTEM_START_DATE validation failed: ...'. In rinzler_proxy the mismatch error names both dates.
variables.audience_reason: It changes the prompt text of a deployed rinzler, and a sidecar must match the serving host. Its main use in the checkout is reproducible capture and replay.

variables.name: SPDLOG_LEVEL

readers.program: libsystem: tron::init_logging. Callers: rinzler and its three variants (src/rinzler.cpp:4547), runtron (src/runtron.cpp:439), and pos_startup_host of the real device library (src/pos/driver.cpp:198)
readers.mechanism: library call spdlog::cfg::load_env_levels(). The getenv is inside spdlog 1.17.0 (include/spdlog/cfg/env.h:28-33 of that library)

variables.values: A comma-separated list. Each entry is either LEVEL, which sets the global level, or NAME=LEVEL, which sets the level of the logger called NAME. LEVEL is one of trace, debug, info, warning (or warn), error (or err), critical, off. Upper and lower case are both accepted. Spaces around names are removed. TRON creates one logger, named default_logger (src/system/spdlog.cpp:53-54).
variables.default: Unset: the logger keeps the level from TRON_LOG_LEVEL. That level is debug when TRON_LOG_LEVEL is unset (src/system/spdlog.cpp:39-43).
variables.invalid_value: An entry with an unknown level name is ignored, with no message. The other entries still apply. Text of 32768 characters or more is ignored as a whole (spdlog include/spdlog/cfg/helpers-inl.h:74, 88).
variables.effect: Changes the level of TRON's logger after TRON_LOG_LEVEL has been applied. It does not change the level of the two outputs (stderr and the log file). They keep the TRON_LOG_LEVEL level (src/system/spdlog.cpp:47, 50). A message is written only if it passes the logger level and also the output level (spdlog include/spdlog/logger.h:262, logger-inl.h:135-137). So SPDLOG_LEVEL can only reduce logging. Example: SPDLOG_LEVEL=warn hides info and debug lines. SPDLOG_LEVEL=trace alone shows nothing more, because the outputs stay at debug.
variables.interactions: TRON_LOG_LEVEL sets the logger level and both output levels first. To get more detail, set TRON_LOG_LEVEL. SPDLOG_LEVEL=off stops all log output, errors included. The entry console=err from the code comment at src/system/spdlog.cpp:59 matches no logger in TRON, so it does nothing. The test launcher of rinzler_proxy removes the variable from the child environment (t/t_rinzler_proxy.cpp:1123).
variables.how_to_check: none found. No log line prints the level in effect. The only sign is which levels appear in the output.
variables.audience_reason: It changes how much a deployed rinzler or runtron logs.
variables.disagreement: Both inventory entries say 'not determined' for the accepted values, for the default, and for how the logger level combines with the output levels. spdlog 1.17.0 is the version that cmake/versions.cmake:5 pins. Its source says: a comma list of LEVEL or NAME=LEVEL; level names trace, debug, info, warning or warn, error or err, critical, off; case is ignored; an empty value is the same as unset; an unknown level name is ignored silently. The variable changes only the logger level. The outputs keep the TRON_LOG_LEVEL level, so the variable can only reduce logging. The example console=err in the code comment matches no TRON logger.

variables.name: SUDO_USER

readers.program: libsystem: pos_heap_setup. The only caller is pos_startup_host of the real device library (src/pos/driver.cpp:290): rinzler, runtron and hardware tests
readers.mechanism: std::getenv. Only presence is tested, and only when the effective user id is 0

variables.values: Any value. Only presence is tested. The text is not parsed.
variables.empty_value: Counts as set. The test is 'not a null pointer'.
variables.invalid_value: Not applicable. No value is invalid.
variables.effect: When the effective user id is 0 and the variable is present, pos_heap_setup logs 'Please do not run as sudo as this will create root-owned files in /dev/hugepages ...' and returns -1. pos_startup_host logs 'pos_startup_host heap_setup failed'. get_devices logs 'INIT: Environment setup failed. Aborting.' and the process exits with code 1 (src/pos/driver.cpp:290-294, 887-889).
variables.interactions: A process that runs as root without the variable is allowed, for example a systemd service or a CI job that runs as root (comment at src/system/memory.cpp:124-127). A process that is not root is never affected. rinzler_proxy, rinzler_mock and rinzler_host never reach this code, because the fake device library does not call pos_heap_setup. The program sudo sets the variable. TRON never sets it.
variables.how_to_check: The error line 'Please do not run as sudo ...' (src/system/memory.cpp:129-133). No line is logged when the check passes.
variables.audience_reason: A person who starts rinzler or runtron with sudo meets this refusal.

variables.name: SYSTEM_CONFIG

readers.program: libpos, the real device library: pos_startup_host (rinzler, runtron, hardware tests)
readers.mechanism: getenv. The whole text is parsed by tron::hardware::system::system_parse_env (src/system/system.cpp:2112)

readers.program: libsystem: parse_instance_from_system_config. Called by early_parse_instance when the command line has no --instance (rinzler and its three variants at src/rinzler.cpp:4563, runtron at src/runtron.cpp:489), and by get_sub_instances
readers.mechanism: std::getenv. Only the --instance option is taken

readers.program: libsystem: system_parse_args (rinzler and its three variants at src/rinzler.cpp:4046, runtron at src/runtron.cpp:248)
readers.mechanism: std::getenv. Reached only under a Dice grant (DICE_DAEMON_CHILD=1)

readers.program: pos_fake, the fake device library: pos_startup_host. Only tests call it. No product program reaches it
readers.mechanism: getenv. The whole text is parsed by system_parse_env

variables.values: Text in command-line form. It is split at white space. A token in double quotes may hold spaces. Inside the quotes a backslash escapes a quote or a backslash (std::quoted, src/system/system.cpp:2074-2081). Options taken (src/system/system.cpp:1954-2052): --instance X,Y or --instance=X,Y (X is the instance index from 0, Y is the instance count, X < Y); --devices LIST (entries like e1:00.0); --app-cores LIST, --dev-cores LIST, --helper-cores LIST (CPU lists like 1,10-14); --numa N; --nr_hugepages N; --hugepage_file PATH; --resource-map PATH; --tracer-core N; --kv-cache-gb N; -o or --optimize; --no-opt; --heap-shadow. A token -- ends the parse. Outside a Dice grant the form --option=value works only for --instance.
variables.default: Unset: nothing is read from the environment, and only the system options from the command line apply. Exception: with DICE_DAEMON_CHILD=1 an unset value fails startup, because --instance is then required (src/pos/driver.cpp:209-224).
variables.empty_value: Outside a Dice grant: parsed as an empty option list. The line 'INIT: environment system config: ' is logged and no option changes. One difference from unset: the resource map is loaded again, so a --resource-map given only on the command line is no longer the loaded map (see interactions). Under a Dice grant: startup fails, as for unset.
variables.invalid_value: Three different results. 1. Clean failure. A wrong --instance form, two --instance options, a bad device list, an empty CPU list, or a missing value at the end of the text make the parse return false. pos_startup_host logs 'INIT: invalid SYSTEM_CONFIG', and get_devices exits the process with code 1 (src/pos/driver.cpp:211-215, 887-889). 2. Process end without that message. Non-numeric text for --numa, --nr_hugepages, --tracer-core or --kv-cache-gb, or inside a CPU list, throws a C++ exception inside a noexcept function, so the process is terminated (src/system/system.cpp:388-405, 2022-2047; src/pos/driver.cpp:191). 3. Silent. A token that is not a known option is ignored with no message, for example a misspelled option or --numa=0.
variables.effect: Gives system placement options to the process through the environment. --instance selects the share of the server (FPGA cards, CPU cores, NUMA node, hugepage files) that the process owns. The real device library parses the whole text during startup, after the command line was parsed. rinzler and runtron also read only the --instance value at program start, when the command line has none. rinzler uses it for the log line label rz<X>/<Y>. rinzler and runtron use it for the /instance-<X> part of the FUSE stats path.
variables.interactions: 1. Order: the command line is parsed first and SYSTEM_CONFIG second. For an option present in both, the SYSTEM_CONFIG value is applied last. 2. POS_1GB_PER_NUMA or POS_NR_HUGEPAGES replace --nr_hugepages afterwards, and POS_HUGEPAGE_PATH replaces --hugepage_file (src/pos/driver.cpp:249-288). 3. Each parse outside a Dice grant loads the resource map again, and the path comes only from the text being parsed (src/system/system.cpp:1911-1936). So when SYSTEM_CONFIG is set and has no --resource-map, a --resource-map from the command line is replaced by the default search. 4. If the command line and SYSTEM_CONFIG both carry --instance with different values, the placement follows SYSTEM_CONFIG, but the log label and the FUSE suffix follow the command line (src/system/system.cpp:1024-1027). This point is read from the code and was not run. 5. Under a Dice grant (DICE_DAEMON_CHILD=1) the command line and SYSTEM_CONFIG are checked together against DICE_SLOTS before anything is applied. --instance must equal the granted instance. The form --option=value is then accepted for every option that takes a value (src/system/system.cpp:1869-1905, 2086-2102). 6. rinzler_proxy, rinzler_mock and rinzler_host do not run the full parse, because the fake get_devices is a stub (src/pos/fake.cpp:398) and no product code calls pos_startup with the fake library. Outside a Dice grant they use only the --instance value: for the log label, and in rinzler_mock and rinzler_host also for the FUSE suffix. Options such as --kv-cache-gb inside SYSTEM_CONFIG have no effect in these three programs. 7. In the real rinzler, --kv-cache-gb here overrides RZ_KV_CACHE_GB. 8. Dice, Slice and the wrappers bin/rinzler and bin/runtron set the variable for the programs they start.
variables.how_to_check: 'INIT: environment system config: <text>' at info level (src/pos/driver.cpp:210, src/pos/fake.cpp:101) shows the text that was parsed. 'Configured instance X,Y using resource map (<path>).' or 'Configured instance X,Y using hardcoded settings.' (src/system/system.cpp:1986-1990) shows the instance in effect. Without an instance: 'INIT: No --instance specified, applying system_optimize() defaults.' (src/system/system.cpp:2065). rinzler log lines carry the label rzX/Y (src/system/spdlog.cpp:86). The rinzler run file holds the instance id and total (src/rinzler.cpp:2491).
variables.audience_reason: It selects which FPGA cards, CPU cores and memory a deployed rinzler or runtron uses.
variables.disagreement: The two inventory files contradict each other on one reader. cpp-pos-system.json names rinzler_proxy, rinzler_mock and rinzler_host as programs that reach the read at src/pos/fake.cpp:99. cpp-rinzler-runtron.json says they do not reach it. The code agrees with cpp-rinzler-runtron.json: only pos_startup (src/pos/fake.cpp:147) calls the fake pos_startup_host, no file under src/ or h/ calls pos_startup for the fake library, and the fake get_devices is a stub (src/pos/fake.cpp:398). Only tests reach src/pos/fake.cpp:99. So in those three programs, options other than --instance inside SYSTEM_CONFIG have no effect outside a Dice grant. Both files also omit the log line 'INIT: environment system config: <text>' (src/pos/driver.cpp:210), which shows the parsed text. All other facts agree.

variables.name: TIKTOKEN_ENCODINGS_BASE

readers.program: harmony_ffi (Rust crate in rust/harmony, linked into librinzler): harmony_encoding_load calls harmony::load_harmony_encoding of the third-party crate openai-harmony 0.0.8
readers.mechanism: third-party library call. The read is std::env::var("TIKTOKEN_ENCODINGS_BASE") at src/tiktoken_ext/public_encodings.rs:128 of openai-harmony, which is not in the checkout

readers.program: librinzler: constructor of tron::harmony::harmony_encoding
readers.mechanism: calls harmony_encoding_load

readers.program: rinzler, rinzler_mock, rinzler_host, rinzler_proxy (all four compile src/rinzler.cpp, src/CMakeLists.txt:95, 115, 152, 180)
readers.mechanism: constructs harmony_encoding one time for each loaded model whose execution slug contains gpt-oss (src/rinzler.cpp:2020)

variables.values: Path to a directory that holds the file o200k_base.tiktoken. The file must have the SHA-256 hash 446a9538cb6c348e3516120d7c08b09f57c36495e2acfffe59a5bf8b0cfb1a2d (openai-harmony src/tiktoken_ext/public_encodings.rs:249-265; the same file name and hash are in bin/slice:1755-1761).
variables.default: Unset: the library uses a cache directory. The cache directory is $TIKTOKEN_RS_CACHE_DIR when that is set, otherwise <temporary directory>/tiktoken-rs-cache. A cached file with the right hash is used. Otherwise the library downloads https://openaipublic.blob.core.windows.net/encodings/o200k_base.tiktoken into the cache and checks the hash (openai-harmony src/tiktoken_ext/public_encodings.rs:128-137, 417-441, 462-479). A host with no cached file and no internet access cannot load a gpt-oss model.
variables.empty_value: Not the same as unset. Rust std::env::var returns the empty text, so the variable counts as set. The library then opens o200k_base.tiktoken in the current working directory of the process and tries no download. This is read from the library source and was not run.
variables.invalid_value: When the variable is set, the library does not fall back to the download. A missing file, an unreadable file or a wrong hash makes the load fail. The harmony_encoding constructor throws harmony_error 'Failed to load Harmony encoding 'HarmonyGptOss': Failed to load encoding: invalid tiktoken vocab file: ...' (src/rinzler/harmony.cpp:220, rust/harmony/src/lib.rs:477). I found no try block around the construction in load_model or around the controller construction in main (src/rinzler.cpp:2137, 4994), so the process ends through the terminate handler. This is read from the code and was not run.
variables.effect: Makes the Harmony tokenizer library read its vocabulary file from the given directory, with a hash check. The download and the shared cache are then not used.
variables.interactions: It matters only when a model whose execution slug contains gpt-oss is loaded. When it is unset, TIKTOKEN_RS_CACHE_DIR and the temporary directory decide where the cache is. bin/slice fetches the file one time and sets the variable for the tests it starts (bin/slice:1844-1876). The packaged rinzler unit does not set it. All facts here depend on the library version. rust/harmony/Cargo.toml:13 pins tag v0.0.8, and rust/harmony/Cargo.lock:1343 pins commit ec7606df9e87e3d0a1fec9f50928c1e407f0c438. Check again when the pin moves (bin/slice:1750-1753 says the same).
variables.how_to_check: none found on success. On failure, the error text 'Failed to load Harmony encoding ...' names the cause.
variables.audience_reason: Needed to load gpt-oss models on a host that cannot download, or to avoid the shared cache.
variables.disagreement: The inventory is right but vague on three points. 1. It does not say what an empty value does: the variable counts as set, and the file is looked for in the current working directory. 2. It does not say that a set variable disables the download fallback, so a missing file or a wrong hash fails the model load. 3. It does not say where the cache is when the variable is unset ($TIKTOKEN_RS_CACHE_DIR or <temporary directory>/tiktoken-rs-cache), or that a cold cache needs internet access. Its evidence can also be stronger: rust/harmony/Cargo.lock:1343 pins the exact commit that I read.

variables.name: TRACE_FILE

readers.program: libpos, the real device library: pos_startup_host (rinzler, runtron, hardware tests)
readers.mechanism: getenv. The text is stored in the global tron::perfetto_trace_dest

variables.values: Either the exact text traced, or a file path. The text is not checked at startup.
variables.default: Unset: the destination stays traced (src/pos/perf.cpp:34). traced means the Perfetto system backend: the process only registers as a producer, and an outside client (perfetto/wrapper or perfetto/tronperf) owns the session and the output file (note at h/common/perfetto.hpp:223-241).
variables.empty_value: Not the same as unset. The destination becomes the empty text. Nothing happens at startup. At the first SIGUSR1 the open of an empty path fails, start_tracing throws inside a noexcept thread function, and the process is terminated (src/pos/perf.cpp:173-175, 248, 273).
variables.invalid_value: A path that cannot be opened for writing gives the same result as an empty value: no error at startup, and process end at the first SIGUSR1.
variables.effect: Sets the process-wide Perfetto trace destination. With a file path, a capture started by the signal SIGUSR1 (10 seconds long) is recorded inside the process and written to that file. The file is opened with O_CREAT and O_TRUNC, mode 0600, at each capture, so each new capture replaces the last one.
variables.interactions: 1. TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES. With TRACE_FILE unset or traced and TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES non-empty, a SIGUSR1 capture throws and ends the process (src/pos/perf.cpp:126-134, 165). With a file path, TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES selects the categories (src/pos/perf.cpp:143-149). 2. runtron --trace and --trace-gen write the same global before the device library starts and pass their own destination to their trace session (src/runtron.cpp:263-267, 295, 342). pos_startup_host runs later and overwrites the global when TRACE_FILE is set. So in runtron the variable changes only later SIGUSR1 captures. This order is read from the code and was not run. 3. rinzler ignores a SIGUSR1 that arrives during a FUSE capture (src/pos/perf.cpp:264-267). 4. Only programs with the real device library read the variable and install the SIGUSR1 tracer (src/pos/driver.cpp:447). rinzler_proxy, rinzler_mock and rinzler_host do not. 5. perfetto/tools/rinzler-capture.sh refuses a target rinzler whose TRACE_FILE is not traced (perfetto/tools/rinzler-capture.sh:208-209).
variables.how_to_check: 'INIT: perfetto trace destination: <text>' at startup, only when the variable is set (src/pos/driver.cpp:229). At each SIGUSR1: 'perfetto tracing starting (<destination>)' at warning level (src/pos/perf.cpp:269).
variables.audience_reason: It is for performance trace capture, not for normal serving. A wrong value can end the process at SIGUSR1.
